@@ -0,0 +1,207 @@ +--- +// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 +// +// "Truthiness portability" — the guide to analyse mode (ADR-022 Part B). A +// FlatBars template renders under ONE engine's truthiness rule, but the same +// template may branch differently on another (Handlebars vs Mustache vs …). +// Analyse mode renders against real data and reports every condition whose branch +// would flip elsewhere, with a portable fix. Every example comes from the one gate-validated source +// (../analyse.mjs, gated by scripts/check-tutorial-tooling.mjs via the engine's +// `analyze`), so the page can never claim a finding the analyser does not produce. +// The normative text lives in docs/ (adr-0022-analyse-mode.adoc). +import Reference from "../layouts/Reference.astro"; +import OpenInLab from "../components/OpenInLab.jsx"; +import { examples as ex } from "../analyse.mjs"; + +const t = (s) => s; // readability helper for inline tag literals + +const groups = [ + { + label: "Truthiness", + items: [ + { href: "#intro", label: "Why truthiness travels badly" }, + { href: "#empty-string", label: "Empty string" }, + { href: "#zero", label: "Zero" }, + { href: "#collections", label: "Empty array & object" }, + { href: "#portable", label: "What's already portable" }, + { href: "#report", label: "The report & JSONata fix" }, + { href: "#using", label: "In the Lab & CI" }, + ], + }, + { + label: "Other references", + items: [ + { href: "/lint", label: "Linting & migration" }, + { href: "/fullbars", label: "FullBars" }, + { href: "/transform", label: "Data shaping" }, + ], + }, + { + label: "Play", + items: [{ href: "/lab/index.html?engine=fullbars", label: "FlatBars Lab ↗" }], + }, +]; +--- + + + + + +
+

Why truthiness travels badly

+

+ A FlatBars template is logic-light, but it still asks yes/no questions: + {t("{{#if bio}}")}, {t("{{#unless items}}")}. The answer + depends on a truthiness rule, and engines disagree. FullBars uses + Handlebars's rule; Mustache, StringTemplate, and others differ. Six values are + the flashpoints — the ambiguous set: +

+
+ falsenull0""[]{t("{}")} +
+

+ false and null are falsy everywhere — portable. The other four are + not: 0 is falsy in Handlebars but truthy in Mustache; + "" the same; [] varies; {t("{}")} is truthy almost + everywhere but falsy under the presence rule. Test one of these in a + condition and your template can render a different branch on someone else's engine. +

+

+ Analyse mode finds these without guessing. It renders your template + against your data through the real engine — byte-identical output, no second + interpreter — and records every truthiness decision, then replays it against the + other named rules. A condition whose branch flips is a portability finding, + reported with a located, rule-free fix. "No findings" on this data is a proof the + render is portable for that data — not a guarantee for all data. +

+
+ + +
+

Empty string

+

+ The user left the field blank, so the value is "". Handlebars treats + that as falsy and shows the {t("{{else}}")} branch; Mustache treats it + as truthy and shows the filled branch — same template, two outputs. +

+ +
+ 1 portability finding. {t("{{#if bio}}")} tested an empty string at + data path bio; it flips under mustache and minimal. + Fix — test it explicitly so the decision doesn't ride on the host's + rule: {t("{{#if (ne bio \"\")}}")}. +
+
+ + +
+

Zero

+

+ 0 is the canonical divergence: falsy in Handlebars, truthy in Mustache + and the minimal/presence rules. "0 unread" silently becomes "all caught up" on the + wrong engine. +

+ +
+ 1 portability finding. {t("{{#if count}}")} tested the number + 0 at data path count. + Fix — includeZero=true keeps it truthy on Handlebars + only (not portable); for every engine, test explicitly: + {t("{{#if (ne count 0)}}")}. +
+
+ + +
+

Empty array & empty object

+

+ An empty array is falsy in Handlebars and Mustache — but the portable spelling + is still to iterate: {t("{{#each}}…{{else}}…{{/each}}")} renders + the empty branch the same way on every engine, without leaning on `if`-falsiness. +

+ +
+ 1 portability finding. {t("{{#if items}}")} tested an empty array. + Fix — iterate: + {t("{{#each items}}…{{else}}empty{{/each}}")}. +
+

+ An empty object is the non-obvious one: truthy in both Handlebars and + Mustache, so it looks safe — but it flips under the presence rule. The + analyser still catches it. +

+ +
+ 1 portability finding. {t("{{#if profile}}")} tested an empty object + at data path profile; it flips under presence. + Fix — test a known key explicitly, e.g. + {t("{{#if profile.name}}")}. +
+
+ + +
+

What's already portable

+

+ Not every condition is a problem. false (and null) are falsy + on every engine, so a condition testing them is safe — the analyser confirms it with a + ✓ line, positive evidence rather than silence. +

+ +
+ 0 portability findings. {t("{{#if active}}")} tested false, + which every rule agrees is falsy. Nothing to fix. +
+
+ + +
+

The report & the JSONata fix

+

+ Each finding is a markdown section: the located tag, the value it tested, the rules + that flip, and a concrete fix that names only helpers that exist + (ne/eq/each). The fixes above are in-template. + When the cleaner fix is in the data, --emit-jsonata generates a + reviewable JSONata scaffold that normalises each offending + bare path out of the ambiguous zone before the data reaches any engine — + e.g. mapping a blank bio to null. It is a scaffold to review, + never applied automatically: what "normalise" means is your call. +

+
+ + +
+

In the Lab & in CI

+

+ In the Lab — Open in Lab on any example above carries the template and + data over; switch to the Truthiness panel beside the output to see the findings + update live as you edit. The ?vendored= corpus turns the Lab into a + portability gallery. +

+

In CI / a script — the same report on the command line:

+ 
$ flatbars analyse template.hbs data.json
+$ flatbars analyse template.hbs data.json --emit-jsonata   # the cleanup scaffold
+

+ The CLI and the Lab share one reportMarkdown through the + flatbars-js bundle, so they can never disagree — and this page's examples + are run through that same analyze in CI, so the findings shown here are + exactly what the engine produces. +

+
+
